content.comment_body: I have two analog inputs and want to choose the highest value to send out through one analog output. Any suggestions?
Hello [user_name], What type of analog signal are you using? Is it 0-10 V or 4-20 mA?
Try using an analog comparator to identify which input is higher, and then apply an analog multiplexer to select that input for output. This kind of setup should work for your application.
Hello [user_name], Additionally, you can compare two analog values as described in the following link: How to compare two analog values with [product_name]? Best regards [user_name]
Dear [user_name], The link you provided does not work, could you please check it?
Hello [user_name], Thanks for your feedback. The link should now work correctly. Here's also the link to the attached file: [document] Best regards [user_name]
Hello, if I have three analog inputs instead of two and want to use the highest value for the analog output, what should I do?
Hello, Which version of [product_name] do you have?

Hi, I loaded the 'select one from three analog inputs' program using [product_name] software (demo version), and when I select the [product_name] with [article_no], I am unable to change the parameters of block B012 MUX. However, if I switch to [article_no], I am able to modify them. Additionally, I cannot connect analog blocks like MUX or arithmetic when creating a new program. Is this a limitation of the demo software?
This is due to the new reference function in [product_name] version [version_no]. [url]
